name: West African Griot
description: Hereditary verbal specialists responsible for historical narration, genealogy, praise, critique, diplomacy, and musical performance. They are the foundational ancestral node of the oral rhythmic continuum.

name: Black American Preaching
description: Church traditions utilizing cadence, vocal inflection, repetition, audience participation, and call-and-response. This established the foundational rhythmic relationship between a speaker and a crowd.

name: Jazz Vocal Improvisation
description: Improvised vocal practices including scat singing and rhythmic manipulation, separating the voice from strict lyrical meaning and treating it as a percussive instrument.

name: Spoken Word and Street Verbal Traditions
description: Performed poetry, verbal competition, the dozens, signifying, and social commentary. This era codified rhythmic street speech as a tool for political and social expression.

name: The Last Poets
description: A collective of poets and musicians arising from the Black Civil Rights movement. Their politically charged, rhythmic spoken-word over minimal drum backing heavily influenced the cadence and subject matter of early MCing.

name: New York Hip Hop Culture
description: The convergence of DJ techniques, extended breakbeats, rhythmic spoken performance, b-boying, and visual art within youth social spaces. This marks the formal synthesis of earlier continuum traditions.

name: Hip Hop MCing
description: Microphone-based performance combining rhythmic speech, rhyme, audience interaction, improvisation, competition, storytelling, and social commentary.

name: Regional Expansion
description: The decentralization of Hip Hop from New York, leading to distinct regional production styles, tempos, and localized slang that built upon the core MCing and DJing traditions.
